verdicts.title: Is p^_w <= p~_w for every admissible w

evidence.title: Gulisashvili 1007.5353
evidence.locator: Sec 4, (55), Lemma 4.1, Thm 4.2, Lemma 4.3, Remark 4.5, example after Cor 4.4
evidence.finding: Statement matches source. Paper shows (57) can fail but gives no counterexample to the conjecture itself. Citing papers (7 on S2, e.g. Gao-Lee 2014) do not address it.

verdicts.residual_statement: My own unverified sketch suggests the answer is NO for pathological w: take w(u)=a_n on [n,n+1) with a_{n+1}=3a_n (smoothed by tiny ramps), S with atoms m_n=exp(-a_{n+1}) at n+1. Then E e^{p w(S)}=sum e^{(p-1)a_{n+1}} gives p~_w=1, while integral of Fbar e^{pw} ~ sum e^{(p-3)a_n} gives p^_w=3 (when ramps are steep enough), so p^>p~ and Piterbarg's formula in its p~ form fails for such w; Thm 4.2 then gives the p^ value. All moments finite, w/log->inf. Needs checking (ramp contributions, call-price realization) before relying.
verdicts.notes: Pure real analysis/probability on a tail function and w; Lean-statable, though the link to implied volatility itself (Black-Scholes inversion limsup) is heavier; the equivalent statement p^<=p~ is elementary. If the sketch holds it is an exercise-level counterexample, not an open problem.

records.title: No-manipulation conditions for nonlinear transient impact (and cross-impact)
records.statement: For $x\mapsto f(x)$ an impact function and $G$ a decay kernel, the transient impact model has price manipulation if a round trip has negative expected cost. Reported resolution (Lee 2026): if $f$ acts on the trading rate before a nonzero integrable Volterra kernel, nonnegative cost on all finite piecewise-constant round trips forces $f$ affine; for $f(x)=\mathrm{sgn}(x)|x|^\delta$, $G(t)=t^{-\gamma}$, $0<\gamma<1$, manipulation exists iff $\delta\neq1$; for monotone readout after the kernel, safety is equivalent to complete positivity of the kernel. Residual not resolved by that paper: multi-asset nonlinear cross-impact.
records.background: Absence of price manipulation constrains admissible impact models used in optimal execution.
known_results: Linear case: no-dynamic-arbitrage iff positive semi-definiteness of kernel (Gatheral; Alfonsi-Schied; Huberman-Stanzl).
Curato-Gatheral-Lillo: convexity of decay is not sufficient for nonlinear impact when gamma+delta>=1.
Schneider-Lillo 2016/19: symmetry necessary for linear cross-impact; permanent nonlinear cross-impact inconsistent with no dynamic arbitrage.

records.title: Which arbitrage-free call surfaces are generated by a continuous martingale
records.statement: Let $(\mu_t)_{t\ge0}$ be a family of probability measures on $\mathbb R$ with constant mean, increasing in convex order (equivalently, call prices $C(K,T)=\int(x-K)^+\mu_T(dx)$ are non-decreasing in $T$ and convex in $K$). Give a necessary and sufficient condition on $(\mu_t)$ for the existence of a martingale $(X_t)$ with continuous paths and $X_t\sim\mu_t$ for all $t$.
records.background: Decides when a static arbitrage-free surface can be fitted by a diffusion-type model and when jumps are unavoidable.
known_results: Kellerer: a Markov martingale (possibly with jumps) with these marginals always exists.

Lowther (arXiv 0808.2319): under weak continuity of t -> mu_t there is a unique strong Markov (almost continuous) fitting martingale; continuity of its paths is shown under extra conditions (convex supports), per secondary sources (Root to Kellerer 1507.07690, 2210.13847; not opened).

records.title: Calendar-spread-free domain of eSSVI parameter functions across the whole surface
records.statement: An eSSVI surface has total implied variance $w(k,T)=\tfrac12\big(\theta_T+\rho_T\psi_T k+\sqrt{(\psi_T k+\theta_T\rho_T)^2+\theta_T^2(1-\rho_T^2)}\big)$ with parameter functions $T\mapsto(\theta_T,\rho_T,\psi_T)$. records.title: Does the expected signature determine the law, for Brownian motion stopped at a domain exit time

records.title: Sharp systemic-event threshold in an equal-split balance-sheet contagion model on sparse random digraphs
records.statement: Let $G_n$ be a sparse directed random graph on $n$ institutions in which each institution splits its exposure equally over its out-neighbours (so adding an out-edge lowers the exposure per edge). For a shock of given size, let $\mathcal S_n$ be the event that a positive fraction of institutions default. Is there a deterministic threshold in the out-degree parameter $\rho_{\rm out}$ at which $\mathbb P(\mathcal S_n)$ jumps from $o(1)$ to $\Omega(1)$ (a sharp threshold), including a description of the critical case $\rho_{\rm out}=1$ and explicit constants? Known: subcritical ($\rho_{\rm out}<1$) cascades are $O((\log n)^2)$ for $c\log n$ shocks; supercritical is covered by a strong-giant/bow-tie theorem; monotone sharp-threshold machinery does not apply because $\mathcal S_n$ is not monotone in the edge set.
records.background: Rigorous contagion thresholds exist for configuration-model networks; the equal-exposure-split sparse digraph model leaves the sharp threshold and critical window unproved.

records.title: Existence of shadow prices for log-optimal investment under proportional costs, multi-asset, continuous time
records.statement: Consider a continuous arbitrage-free multi-asset (d>=2) price process $S$ with proportional transaction costs $\lambda>0$ and a log-utility investor. Does a shadow price (a frictionless price process $\tilde S$ inside the bid-ask spread yielding the same optimal strategy and utility) exist? Known: counterexample in discrete time even with bounded prices; existence if short selling is prohibited (Benedetti-Campi-Kallsen-Muhle-Karbe); a shadow price exists for continuous one-dimensional processes under NUPBR (Czichowsky-Schachermayer-Yang); a generalized "sandwiched" shadow price exists for general cadlag processes. The multi-asset continuous-time case with short selling was not found in the sources read.
records.background: Shadow prices reduce friction problems to frictionless ones.
known_results: Czichowsky-Muhle-Karbe-Schachermayer 2014: counterexample in discrete time.

records.title: Sharp no-asymptotic-arbitrage conditions for large financial markets
records.statement: Kabanov-Kramkov (1998) characterize no asymptotic arbitrage of the first kind (NAA1) as contiguity of the objective measures $(P^n)$ with respect to the sets of equivalent (local) martingale measures $(Q^n)$, and NAA2 as contiguity of the lower envelopes of equivalent martingale measures with respect to $(P^n)$, with Hellinger-process criteria. Klein-Schachermayer extend to non-complete markets and later work (Klein; Cuchiero-Klein-Teichmann) relates NAA1 to no-unbounded-profit-with-bounded-risk. The sharp-conditions question is therefore solved in the sense of necessary and sufficient contiguity characterizations.

records.title: Robust hedging duality for American options with irregular (non-cadlag) obstacle under semimartingale-characteristic uncertainty
records.statement: Work in the nondominated framework of Rodrigues: a family $\mathcal P$ of laws on path space under which the canonical price process $S$ is a semimartingale with characteristics constrained to a prescribed measurable set-valued map. Let $\xi=(\xi_t)_{t\le T}$ be an American-option payoff process (adapted, class (D)) that is NOT assumed cadlag. Rodrigues proves, for cadlag class (D) obstacles, an aggregator $Y$ of the family of Snell envelopes $Y^P_t=\operatorname{ess\,sup}_{\tau\ge t}E^P[\xi_\tau\mid\mathcal G_t]$ and the hedging duality $\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\sup_{\tau}E^P[\xi_\tau]=\inf\{x:\exists\text{ superhedge } x+Z\cdot S\ge\xi\ \mathcal P\text{-q.s. on a stopping-time-by-stopping-time basis}\}$ with a minimal hedging strategy. Question: does an aggregator of the Snell envelopes, and hence the duality with minimal hedge, still exist when $\xi$ is an arbitrary optional process (and, separately, on random or unbounded horizons)? The obstruction identified is (i) measurability of the Snell envelope in the law parameter without the penalised-BSDE approximation and (ii) an optional decomposition for cadlag (not right-continuous-filtration) supermartingales.
records.background: American-option superhedging under uncertainty is the natural dynamic-stopping extension of robust hedging duality; regularity of the payoff is the remaining technical gap in the semimartingale-characteristics framework.
known_results: Rodrigues (2025): aggregator of Snell envelopes and robust hedging duality for cadlag class-(D) American payoffs in general semimartingale (jumps allowed, non-vanishing diffusion) uncertainty.

records.title: Duality l(L^infty)=E' for the robust multi-period binomial model
records.statement: Let $\mathcal P$ be a convex set of probability measures on a measurable space $(\Omega,\mathcal F)$. Let $E$ be the space of finite signed measures absolutely continuous with respect to at least one $P\in\mathcal P$ (total variation norm), let $L^\infty=L^\infty(\mathcal P)$ be the space of $\mathcal P$-quasi-surely bounded measurable functions modulo $\mathcal P$-q.s. equality, and let $l:L^\infty\to E'$, $l_h(\mu)=\int h\,d\mu$. The map $l$ is an isometric embedding with weak$^*$-dense range, and the question is whether the range is all of $E'$. For $T=1$ and the robust binomial model of Blanchard--Carassus (parameter box $(u,d,\pi)\in E_0$, $\Omega=(0,\infty)$, $S_1=S_0Y_1$), one has $l(L^\infty)=E'$ on a canonical extension of the model (Klein--Köstenberger). Question: for $T>1$, does the robust multi-period binomial model of Blanchard--Carassus (uncertainty set generated by the same parameter box at each of the $T$ steps), or any non-trivial robust multi-period binomial model, satisfy $l(L^\infty)=E'$ (on the model or on its extension)? A proof or a counterexample settles it. The exact uncertainty set is the one fixed in the cited papers.
records.background: The quantitative Halmos--Savage theorems and the robust FTAP for large financial markets of Cuchiero--Klein--Köstenberger--Schmidt assume l(L^infty)=E'; without it the multi-period extension of their robust asymptotic-arbitrage theory is not available.
known_results: For T=1, l(L^infty)=E' holds for the robust binomial model after a canonical extension (Klein--Köstenberger, arXiv 2605.04912, Section 5.3 and Corollary 46).
l(L^infty) is always weak* dense in E' (Lemma 3.4 of arXiv 2504.06686), so the issue is weak* closedness.

Klein--Köstenberger (Lemma 40, Remark 41) show the supports of the T=1 sub-families are not disjoint in general and that this already occurs for multi-period; the disjoint-support route of the one-period proof therefore does not transfer directly.

records.title: CLT for the spot-variance-based roughness estimator beyond the rough regime (H >= 3/4)
records.statement: In the model of Chong--Hoffmann--Liu--Rosenbaum--Szymanski, the latent spot variance is $c_t=c_0+\int g_H(t-s)\,\eta_s\,dW_s+\dots$ with kernel $g_H(t)=K_H^{-1}t_+^{H-1/2}$ near $0$ and the log-price $x$ is observed at mesh $\delta_n\to0$. records.statement:

records.title: Do law-determined norm inequalities imply complete mixability?
records.statement: Let $F$ have mean $\mu$ and $s=(n\mu-t)/(n-1)$. records.title: Piterbarg's conjecture on the implied-volatility lim sup when all moments are finite
records.statement: Let $C$ be a call-price function of an asset price $S_T$ with all moments finite ($\tilde p=\infty$), maturity $T$, implied volatility $I(K)$, and $w$ a positive increasing function with Gulisashvili's growth condition (48). Piterbarg conjectured $\limsup_{K\to\infty} I(K)\sqrt{w(K)}/\sqrt{\log K}=1/\sqrt{2T\tilde p_w}$ with $\tilde p_w=\sup\{p\ge0:\int_0^\infty e^{pw(u)}\,d[-\bar F_T(u)]<\infty\}$. Gulisashvili proves the formula with $\hat p_w=\sup\{p:\int_0^\infty\bar F_T(u)e^{pw(u)}du<\infty\}$ in place of $\tilde p_w$ (and $\tilde p_w\le\hat p_w$ always), and the original form under a mild extra condition on $w$. Question: is $\hat p_w\le\tilde p_w$ (equivalently, Piterbarg's formula) true for every admissible $w$ and every call-price function, or is there a counterexample?
